title: Solar-Powered Internet Hubs and Progressive Web Applications for Sustainable Digital Education in Remote Areas
content: Access to digital education remains uneven in remote regions due to unstable electricity infrastructure and limited internet connectivity. While solar-powered systems can address energy constraints and Progressive Web Applications (PWAs) can support offline-capable learning platforms, limited research has examined their integration as a unified solution for sustainable digital education. This study proposes and evaluates an integrated model combining solar-powered internet hubs with a PWA-based learning system to improve digital learning access in remote educational environments. This research employed a design-based research (DBR) approach consisting of three phases: contextual needs analysis, system design and development, and pilot implementation. The pilot intervention was conducted over 12 weeks in a remote vocational secondary school involving 78 students and 8 teachers. Data were collected through system performance logs, platform analytics, pre–post digital literacy assessments, student surveys, and qualitative feedback from teachers and students. The solar-powered hub achieved stable operation with a system uptime of 94.6%. The PWA platform demonstrated strong performance, including a local response time of 0.82 seconds and an offline access success rate of 98.3%. Student engagement increased significantly, with weekly logins rising by 155%, assignment completion improving from 62% to 87%, and average session duration increasing by 108%. Digital literacy scores also improved significantly, with a mean increase of 22.5 points (p < .01). In addition, the proportion of students with reliable daily digital access increased from 53% to 92%, indicating improved digital equity. The integration of solar-powered internet infrastructure and PWA-based learning platforms provides a sustainable and resilient approach to supporting digital education in remote areas by improving connectivity reliability, student engagement, digital literacy, and equitable access to learning resources.
